title: Timezone boundary + out-of-order ingestion causing transient double-counts in per-model usage charts
creator: Marco Li
description: Summary: Several customers reported brief, unexplained increases in per-model token and embedding counts around midnight UTC and during DST transitions. Investigation shows a sequence of contributing issues: (1) some ingestion sources emit events with local timezone timestamps (without normalized UTC), (2) our late-event/backfill ingestion path accepts events with timestamps in the future of the aggregation window, and (3) rate-limit retry behavior re-emits identical request events with new event_ids, leading to duplicate counting when backfills and retries overlap. The combined effect produces transient double-counts and small negative deltas after reconciliation. This ticket defines the diagnosis, fixes in the ingestion and aggregation pipelines, and a safe rollout + reconciliation strategy.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate client sending generation events with local timestamps set to 'YYYY-MM-DDT23:58:xx+01:00' (no UTC normalization).
2) Trigger a simulated rate-limit retry that re-submits the same generation with a new event_id and slightly later timestamp (e.g., +00:02).
3) Run the backfill consumer which accepts late events and inserts them into the raw-timeseries table without deduplication or watermark checks.
4) Observe the console per-model hourly chart: a spike at the late-event hour and a small negative correction when reconciliation runs next day.
investigation_logs: 2026-03-02: Triage — received user report from Customer Success (acct: acme-ml) showing +18% spike at 00:00 UTC on 2026-02-28.
2026-03-03: Correlated spike with ingestion logs — found events with timezone offsets in payloads (e.g., +01:00) and no normalization to UTC at edge.

2026-03-04: Found ~12% of affected events originated from SDK versions < 1.9 that did not set 'timestamp_utc' header. Also saw retry patterns from gateway with new event_ids when rate-limit 429 responses occurred.

2026-03-05: Aggregation team confirmed backfill consumer inserts late events into aggregation table with only a dedup key of (customer, model, hour) which is insufficient when identical calls are retried with new ids.
2026-03-09: Reproduced locally using synthetic stream; observed transient double-counts and small negative corrections after reconciliation run.
root_cause_analysis: Missing UTC normalization at ingestion — several upstream SDKs and partners emit local-timestamp fields that are not converted to a canonical UTC timestamp before downstream processing.
Backfill consumer accepts 'future' timestamps relative to aggregation watermark and inserts them into hourly buckets without enforcing watermark/late-window limits.
Retry duplicate events are given new event_ids by the gateway; our current dedupe uses event_id only, so retried requests bypass dedupe and get counted twice.
Aggregation logic allows insertion of late events into past buckets which creates spikes; reconciliation later subtracts what it thinks is duplicate, causing negative corrections in chart deltas.
UI smoothing highlights these transient artifacts, which confuses customers and triggers support tickets.
decision: Normalize timestamps at the ingestion edge to a canonical 'received_utc' before any downstream processing; prefer server-received UTC over client-supplied local timestamps when present.

Introduce a watermarking policy per-customer: only accept backfill events with timestamp <= now + 5m and >= now - 7d. Events outside the window go to a quarantine topic for manual review/reconciliation.

Improve deduplication to use (canonicalized_event_signature, customer, model, request_hash) where canonicalized_event_signature derived from call payload + client_request_id if present. This ensures retry-with-new-event-id does not double-count.
Add idempotency hooks to the gateway so retries reuse original event_signature when possible.

Enhance aggregation to compute token counts using monotonic counters when available and ignore tiny negative corrections in UI smoothing; surface a 'backfill' badge on chart points that were modified by reconciliation.
implementation_plan: A. Ingestion edge (edge-service): add middleware to parse timezone offsets and set 'ingest_received_utc' header. If client timestamp present, compute canonical UTC and store both client_ts and canonical_ts.
B. Gateway: extend request metadata to include client_request_id and original_event_signature; on retry, maintain original_event_signature when payload identical.
C. Backfill consumer: enforce watermark window; route out-of-window events to quarantine topic and add extra dedupe layer using request_hash in addition to event_id.
D. Aggregation service: change dedupe key to include request_hash/canonical_signature and add idempotent upsert path. Add metric: 'duplicate_events_rejected'.
E. Console UI: ignore negative delta adjustments less than 0.5% of hourly bucket when smoothing; add a small indicator on affected points with a tooltip explaining backfill reconciliation.
F. Data migration: run a reconciliation job for the last 14 days for tenants with spikes to dedupe duplicates based on newly computed request_hashes and re-compute per-model hourly aggregates.
G. Rollout via feature flag: enable ingestion changes in canary region (us-west-2) for 48 hours, then expand to 10% of tenants before full rollout.
testing_and_qa_criteria: Unit tests: timezone parsing and canonicalization for a variety of offsets and DST transitions.
Integration tests: retry scenarios where gateway resubmits requests with new event_id but identical payload — ensure dedupe prevents double-counting.
Load test: ingestion path with 10k events/s including 2% out-of-order events — aggregation correctness should hold and latency SLOs met.
Backfill acceptance tests: events outside watermark should land in quarantine topic and not affect hourly aggregates.
UI test: chart smoothing does not show negative blips > 0.5% and backfill badge appears on modified points.
Manual verification: run reconciliation for a seeded tenant and confirm chart aligns to expected single-count totals.
rollback_plan: If duplicates increase after rollout, toggle feature flag to revert new dedupe behavior on gateway and ingestion (can revert within 15 minutes).
If reconciliation job produces unexpected drops, pause and revert to snapshot-backed restore of the affected aggregation partitions and investigate logs.
Quarantine topic will contain any out-of-window events so rollback will not lose data — manual reingest path available.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metric: duplicate_events_rejected (per-customer) — alert if > 0.5% of total events for 5m.
New dashboard: ingestion-timestamp-origin (client_ts vs ingest_received_utc) and fraction of events with missing client_request_id.
Alert: sudden >10% hour-over-hour change in per-model token counts for a tenant with tag 'sensitive' — route to on-call telemetry pager.
Post-rollout check: compare canary tenants' hourly aggregates before/after rollout and ensure < 0.2% variance for steady workloads.
